180.economics: 10 FAE/block, 600k era, 12m hard ceiling; scheduled integer-atom issuance 11,999,999.922 FAE
180.propagation: historical reported P95 ~0.128s in failed V1/V2 runs; provenance/raw-bundle gap; not PASS
180.daa: direct active-v4 evidence: 20-block discrete integer-bit retarget; honest 0.1x–10x shocks converge, but quantization envelope 127.3–254.6s and stochastic mean drift/retarget noise produce WARN
180.timestamp: active +120s rule is DAA-sensitive; no relative reward-share advantage demonstrated in paired model; WARN
180.small_miner: best event frequency / lowest payout-count variance of compared targets; absolute lumpiness remains for very small shares

300.economics: 14 FAE/block, 430k era, 12.04m hard ceiling, 200-block maturity in candidate package
300.propagation: v2 real three-region WAN: 500 samples, P50 0.100s, mean 0.111458s, P95 0.116s
300.daa: v2 ASERT-style research proxy showed lowest noise / fastest proxy recovery among 300/600/900, but this algorithm is not the active 180s DAA and is not activation authority
300.timestamp: no active-mainnet authority; candidate hardening work is separate
300.small_miner: lower reward-event frequency and higher variance than 180 at fixed share; less timing pressure for propagation/outage

600.economics: 28 FAE/block only when referring to the v2 calendar+supply-neutral branch; not a newly selected economic package
600.propagation: v2 real three-region WAN: 500 samples, P50 0.111s, mean 0.12164s, P95 0.13805s
600.daa: v2 ASERT-style research proxy only; not direct evidence for an active 600s consensus implementation
600.timestamp: not separately activated or validated as an active rule here
600.small_miner: lowest reward-event frequency / highest payout-count variance of compared targets; least fixed-delay race/outage pressure

tradeoffs.interpretation: 180 improves expected user wait and solo reward-event frequency, but confirmation count is not normalized security.
Arithmetic capacity only; real throughput depends on block payload, relay, validation and demand.

tradeoffs.direction: 180 lower than 300 lower than 600 at equal expected issuance
tradeoffs.interpretation: Supports household/solo participation, but does not eliminate pool pressure at very small hash share.

tradeoffs.direction: 180 higher than 300 higher than 600 for fixed absolute delay
tradeoffs.interpretation: Shorter timing increases first-order low-latency advantage; direct FAE revenue evidence remains missing.

tradeoffs.direction: 180 higher probability of competing blocks during a given outage
tradeoffs.interpretation: The 208s V2 failure is more consequential at 180s, but causality was not established.

tradeoffs.direction: 180 has direct implementation-specific evidence; 300/600 v2 evidence uses a different research proxy
tradeoffs.interpretation: Cross-target DAA comparison is not apples-to-apples and must remain qualified.
Zero observed events without adequate admitted denominators/tails is not safety proof.

>=500 admitted propagation samples with P50/mean/P95 and P99 when available
statistically sufficient natural stale/fork denominator meeting frozen Wilson gates
